Organizational  Leadership  Chartered  Association  Event  for  Voting  Delegates  Event  Category:  Leadership
……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  one  competitor  This  event  is  designed  for  chartered  associations  to  use  as  a  possible  option  for  selecting  voting  delegates  for  ILC.    
New  for  2026-2027
 The  Organizational  Leadership  test  will  now  have  50  test  questions.  Editorial  updates  have  been  made.   
Event  Summary
 The  purpose  of  the  event  is  two-fold:  1)  To  assist  Chartered  Associations  with  selecting  their  Voting  Delegates  if  a  method  
does
 
not
 
already
 
exist
 
and
 
2)
 
To
 
encourage
 
HOSA
 
members
 
to
 
develop
 
and
 
apply
 
their
 
knowledge
 
of
 
the
 
HOSA

Parliamentary
 
Procedure
 
to
 
represent
 
their
 
Chartered
 
Associations
 
at
 
the
 
International
 
Leadership
 
Conference
 
as
 
an
 
ofﬁcial
 
Voting
 
Delegate.
   
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  an  eraser  for  test HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Voting  Delegate  Selection  Process  
At  the  Chartered  Association  level,  the  selection  of  a  Voting  Delegate  is  at  the  State  Advisor's  discretion  or  as  outlined  by  the  Chartered  Association’s  Bylaws  and/or  Policies  and  Procedures.  HOSA  members  interested  in  serving  as  Voting  Delegates  for  their  Chartered  Association  should  check  with  their  State  Advisor  to  determine  the  process  used  in  their  Chartered  Association.  
Optional  HOSA  Voting  Delegate  Test  
●  If  a  selection  process  is  not  clearly  outlined  in  the  Chartered  Association’s  Bylaws  and/or  Policies  and  Procedures,  the  Chartered  Association  may  use  the  HOSA  Voting  Delegate  Test  as  a  selection  method.   ●  If  used,  the  HOSA  Voting  Delegate  test  shall  consist  of  a  50-item  multiple-choice  test  and  one  essay  question.  The  written  test  will  measure  knowledge  and  understanding  of  the  information  required  to  be  a  voting  delegate.  Competitors  will  have  60  minutes  to  complete  the  test.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  the  essay  will  be  judged  to  break  the  tie.  
References   The  references  below  are  used  to  develop  the  test  questions:  ●  HOSA  Handbook, Sections  A,  B,  and  C  ●  HOSA  Website ●  Robert's  Rules  of  Order  Newly  Revised  in  Brief  3
 rd
 Edition. ●  First  Fifty  Years  1976-2026  HOSA  Publication. 
 
 Organizational  Leadership  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  3  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Written  Test  Plan  The  test  plan  for  the  Organizational  Leadership  Test  is:  ●  Voting  Delegate  Role  and  Responsibilities-  24%  ●  Parliamentary  Procedure-  24%  ●  HOSA  Inc.-  16%  ●  Organizational  Structure  of  HOSA-  12%  ●  History  of  HOSA-  12%  ●  Positions  and  Responsibilities  of  the  Executive  Council-  8%  ●  Membership-  4%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  HOSA  has  how  many  regions?  A.  Two  B.  Three  C.  Four  D.  Five  2.  A  member  who  is  NOT  in  favor  of  a  motion  votes  by  saying:  A.  nay.  B.  no.  C.  negative.  D.  nothing.  3.   Under  what  circumstances  can  a  parliamentary  motion  to  Postpone  Indeﬁnitely  be  used  by  a  member?  A.  To  postpone  the  motion  to  a  later  time  B.  To  change  a  motion  to  make  it  more  germane  C.  To  dispose  of  an  embarrassing  main  motion  D.  To  postpone  the  motion  until  the  next  meeting

Voting  Delegate  Responsibilities  
1.  Each  Chartered  Association  will  implement  a  process  for  notifying  the  Voting  Delegates  who  have  been  selected  for  this  important  role.   2.  Voting  Delegate  ILC  Requirements:  Before  the  ILC,  Voting  Delegates  must  r eview  the  following  materials:  a.  Voting  Delegate  Packet:  All  Voting  Delegates  attending  the  ILC  will  read  the  Voting  Delegate  Packet.  Voting  Delegates  will  receive  the  Voting  Delegate  Packet  from  their  State  Advisor.  State  Advisors  receive  the  Voting  Delegate  Packet  60  days  before  the  ILC  from  HOSA  Headquarters.  b.  Executive  Council  Applicant  Resumes  and  YouTube  Videos:  All  voting  delegates  attending  the  ILC  must  read  the  Executive  Council  Applicants’  resumes and  the  YouTube  videos  on  HOSA’s  website  at  www.hosa.org should  be  watched  before  coming  to  the  HOSA  ILC.  3.  At  the  International  Leadership  Conference,  Voting  Delegates  must  attend  and  participate  in  the  following  events  to  fulﬁll  their  duties  as  a  Voting  Delegate:   a.  Voting  Delegate  Orientation   b.  Meet  the  Candidates  Breakfast   c.  Chartered  Association  Caucus  –  if  desired  d.  Business  Session  e.  Recognition  Session  
                           
 *Check  the  ILC  schedule  for  exact  dates  and  times  for  these  events!   4.  At  the  International  Leadership  Conference,  Voting  Delegates  who  represent  their  Chartered  Association  will  be  recognized  with  a  voting  delegate  ribbon,  certiﬁcate,  and  pin.    
Future  Opportunities  The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
